sources: Lean 4 theorem prover, https://lean-lang.org (core library only, no Mathlib)
lean/Main.lean (this repository): the spindrift-check command-line checker

how_to_check: cd lean && lake build && lake env lean Check.lean && .lake/build/bin/spindrift-check --selftest
note: Each theorem is proved for any field (or commutative ring) of characteristic 0, so it holds for the real numbers. Lean checks the algebra of the formulas; it does not check measured values. That note is about the physics theorems (lean/SpinDrift/Physics.lean). The checker theorems (Checker.lean, Soundness.lean) prove what the three verdicts of SpinDrift.verdict mean for exact natural-number fractions; the compiled spindrift-check binary runs those definitions for POST /api/verdict.

checker.rule: NOT_MET if some requirement with every input present is violated; otherwise NEED_MORE_INFORMATION if some requirement has a missing input; otherwise REQUIREMENTS_MET
checker.requirement: prod lhs <= prod rhs over non-negative fractions num/den (den > 0), decided by cross-multiplication in Nat; a missing factor (?) or a zero denominator leaves it undecided
checker.input_format: lines 'check <id>' and 'req <id> <factors> <= <factors>'; factor n/d, n or ?

theorems.name: nv_splitting
theorems.doc: The two lines split by `2γB`: the field is read from the splitting.
theorems.statement: {α : Type} [CommRing α] (D γ B : α) : nuPlus D γ B - nuMinus D γ B = 2 * (γ * B)
theorems.section: NV centre in diamond: optically detected magnetic resonance (Barry et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004, Eq. 6)
theorems.used_in: NV console: field from the ODMR splitting

theorems.name: nv_centre
theorems.doc: The pair stays centred on the zero-field splitting `D`.
theorems.statement: {α : Type} [CommRing α] (D γ B : α) : nuPlus D γ B + nuMinus D γ B = 2 * D
theorems.section: NV centre in diamond: optically detected magnetic resonance (Barry et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004, Eq. 6)
theorems.used_in: NV console: line pair centred on D

theorems.name: nv_zero_field
theorems.doc: At zero field both lines sit at `D` (2870 MHz).
theorems.statement: {α : Type} [CommRing α] (D γ : α) : nuPlus D γ 0 = D ∧ nuMinus D γ 0 = D
theorems.section: NV centre in diamond: optically detected magnetic resonance (Barry et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004, Eq. 6)
theorems.used_in: NV console: both lines at 2870 MHz at zero field

theorems.name: opm_steady_state
theorems.doc: Sulai's Eq. B2 (transverse field only) solves the steady-state Bloch equations: `P_x = RΩ/(Γ² + Ω²)`, `P_z = RΓ/(Γ² + Ω²)`. This also fixes the sign of the `P_z` numerator (`+Γ²`).
theorems.section: Optically pumped magnetometer: Bloch steady state (Sulai et al., arXiv 1906.03227, Eqs. B1-B2)
theorems.used_in: OPM console: Bloch steady state P_x, P_z

theorems.name: bloch_circle
theorems.doc: In units of the half width (`x = Ω/Γ`), the tip of the polarisation traces a circle of radius ½ centred at `(0, ½)`: `p_x² + (p_z − ½)² = ¼` with `p_x = x/(1+x²)`, `p_z = 1/(1+x²)`.
theorems.section: Optically pumped magnetometer: Bloch steady state (Sulai et al., arXiv 1906.03227, Eqs. B1-B2)
theorems.used_in: OPM console: polarisation tip on a circle (Bloch sphere view)

theorems.name: opm_half_width
theorems.doc: The Lorentzian `1/(1+x²)` falls to half its peak at `x = 1`, so `ΔB = Γ/γ` is the half width at half maximum.
theorems.section: Optically pumped magnetometer: Bloch steady state (Sulai et al., arXiv 1906.03227, Eqs. B1-B2)
theorems.used_in: OPM console: resonance half width at x = 1

theorems.name: fret_half
theorems.doc: Förster efficiency is exactly ½ at the Förster radius (`r = R₀`).
theorems.statement: {α : Type} [Field α] [IsCharP α 0] (R₀ : α) (_h : R₀ ^ 6 ≠ 0) : R₀ ^ 6 / (R₀ ^ 6 + R₀ ^ 6) = 1 / 2
theorems.section: Quantum-dot FRET (FRET-Calc, Comput. Phys. Commun. 2023, Eqs. 2-3)
theorems.used_in: Quantum-dot console: E = 1/2 at r = R0

theorems.name: fret_one_acceptor
theorems.doc: The multi-acceptor form (Eq. 3) reduces to Eq. 2 for one acceptor.
theorems.statement: {α : Type} [Field α] (R₀ r : α) : (1 * R₀ ^ 6) / (1 * R₀ ^ 6 + r ^ 6) = R₀ ^ 6 / (R₀ ^ 6 + r ^ 6)
theorems.section: Quantum-dot FRET (FRET-Calc, Comput. Phys. Commun. 2023, Eqs. 2-3)
theorems.used_in: Quantum-dot console: n = 1 acceptor form

theorems.name: fret_inverse
theorems.doc: Inversion used for the measured points: if `E = 1/(1+q)` with `q = (r/R₀)⁶`, then `q = 1/E − 1`.
theorems.section: Quantum-dot FRET (FRET-Calc, Comput. Phys. Commun. 2023, Eqs. 2-3)
theorems.used_in: Quantum-dot console: distance from measured efficiency

theorems.name: snr_averaging
theorems.doc: Averaging law without square roots: if the averaged noise `a` satisfies `a²·N = n²` (that is `a = n/√N`), then the averaged SNR satisfies `(A/a)² = (A/n)²·N`, i.e. SNR grows as √N.
theorems.statement: {α : Type} [Field α] (A a n N : α) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hn : n ≠ 0) (h : a ^ 2 * N = n ^ 2) : (A / a) ^ 2 = (A / n) ^ 2 * N
theorems.used_in: NV console: SNR grows as the square root of beats averaged

theorems.name: field_clash
theorems.doc: Field clash: the NV bias (1 mT = 1 000 000 nT) over the OPM range (5 nT) is 200 000.
theorems.used_in: Tower: NV bias versus OPM range

theorems.name: odmr_step_vs_rpeak
theorems.doc: ODMR-Lab's field step (0.05 mT = 50 000 000 pT) over a 25 pT heartbeat R-peak is 2 000 000.
theorems.used_in: NV console: simulator step versus heartbeat R-peak

theorems.name: usable_eq_some_iff
theorems.doc: A factor is usable exactly when it is present with a positive denominator.
theorems.statement: {f : Option Q} {a : Q} : usable f = some a ↔ f = some a ∧ 0 < a.den
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: usable_eq_none_iff
theorems.doc: A factor is unusable exactly when it is missing or has a zero denominator.
theorems.statement: (f : Option Q) : usable f = none ↔ MissingFactor f
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: prod_eq_some_iff
theorems.doc: The executable product agrees with the specification `Denotes`.
theorems.statement: {fs : List (Option Q)} {q : Q} : prod fs = some q ↔ Denotes fs q
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: prod_eq_none_iff
theorems.doc: The product is undefined exactly when some factor is missing or malformed.
theorems.statement: {fs : List (Option Q)} : prod fs = none ↔ ∃ f ∈ fs, MissingFactor f
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Denotes.den_pos
theorems.doc: Exact products of present, well-formed factors have a positive denominator.
theorems.statement: {fs : List (Option Q)} {q : Q} (h : Denotes fs q) : 0 < q.den
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: holds_true_iff
theorems.doc: Lean says a requirement holds exactly when the specification `Holds` is true.
theorems.statement: (r : Req) : holds r = some true ↔ Holds r
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: a requirement's holds = true

theorems.name: holds_false_iff
theorems.doc: Lean says a requirement is violated exactly when every input is present and `lhs > rhs` (`Violated`).
theorems.statement: (r : Req) : holds r = some false ↔ Violated r
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: a requirement's holds = false

theorems.name: holds_none_iff
theorems.doc: Lean leaves a requirement undecided exactly when some input is missing or malformed (`Missing`).
theorems.statement: (r : Req) : holds r = none ↔ Missing r
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: a requirement's holds = null (missing input)

theorems.name: missing_never_decides
theorems.doc: Missing data never becomes a pass or a fail: one missing factor leaves the requirement undecided.
theorems.statement: {r : Req} (h : none ∈ r.lhs ∨ none ∈ r.rhs) : holds r = none
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: missing, NOT_STATED and TO_CONFIRM inputs are sent as ? and never pass or fail

theorems.name: zero_den_never_decides
theorems.doc: A malformed factor (zero denominator) never becomes a pass or a fail either.
theorems.statement: {r : Req} {q : Q} (hq : q.den = 0) (h : some q ∈ r.lhs ∨ some q ∈ r.rhs) : holds r = none
theorems.tactics: term: (holds_none_iff r).2 ⟨some q, List.mem_append.2 h, .inr ⟨q, rfl, hq⟩⟩
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: holds_violated_exclusive
theorems.doc: A requirement cannot both hold and be violated.
theorems.statement: {r : Req} (h1 : Holds r) (h2 : Violated r) : False
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: missing_never_passes_or_fails
theorems.doc: A requirement with a missing input is neither met nor violated.
theorems.statement: {r : Req} (h : Missing r) : ¬ Holds r ∧ ¬ Violated r
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: verdict_met_iff
theorems.doc: REQUIREMENTS_MET exactly when Lean says every requirement holds.
theorems.statement: (rs : List Req) : verdict rs = .met ↔ ∀ r ∈ rs, holds r = some true
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: REQUIREMENTS_MET exactly when every requirement holds

theorems.name: verdict_notMet_iff
theorems.doc: NOT_MET exactly when some requirement with every input present is violated.
theorems.statement: (rs : List Req) : verdict rs = .notMet ↔ ∃ r ∈ rs, holds r = some false
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: verdict_needInfo_iff
theorems.doc: NEED_MORE_INFORMATION exactly when no requirement is violated and some requirement has a missing input.
theorems.statement: (rs : List Req) : verdict rs = .needInfo ↔ (∀ r ∈ rs, holds r ≠ some false) ∧ ∃ r ∈ rs, holds r = none
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: verdict_notMet_sound
theorems.doc: NOT_MET implies a requirement with every input present is violated.
theorems.statement: {rs : List Req} (h : verdict rs = .notMet) : ∃ r ∈ rs, holds r = some false
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: NOT_MET names a requirement violated with every input present

theorems.name: verdict_needInfo_sound
theorems.doc: NEED_MORE_INFORMATION implies no requirement is violated and some requirement has a missing input.
theorems.statement: {rs : List Req} (h : verdict rs = .needInfo) : (∀ r ∈ rs, holds r ≠ some false) ∧ ∃ r ∈ rs, holds r = none
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: NEED_MORE_INFORMATION means nothing violated and an input missing

theorems.name: verdict_met_spec
theorems.doc: REQUIREMENTS_MET exactly when every requirement holds in the specification.
theorems.statement: (rs : List Req) : verdict rs = .met ↔ ∀ r ∈ rs, Holds r
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: REQUIREMENTS_MET against the independent specification

theorems.name: verdict_notMet_spec
theorems.doc: NOT_MET implies a documented violation: every input of that requirement is present and `lhs > rhs`.
theorems.statement: {rs : List Req} (h : verdict rs = .notMet) : ∃ r ∈ rs, Violated r
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: NOT_MET implies a documented violation

theorems.name: verdict_notMet_complete
theorems.doc: A documented violation always gives NOT_MET.
theorems.statement: {rs : List Req} (h : ∃ r ∈ rs, Violated r) : verdict rs = .notMet
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: verdict_needInfo_spec
theorems.doc: NEED_MORE_INFORMATION implies nothing is violated in the specification and some requirement lacks an input.
theorems.statement: {rs : List Req} (h : verdict rs = .needInfo) : (∀ r ∈ rs, ¬ Violated r) ∧ ∃ r ∈ rs, Missing r
theorems.tactics: obtain ⟨h1, r, hr, hn⟩ := verdict_needInfo_sound h
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: NEED_MORE_INFORMATION against the independent specification

theorems.name: missing_blocks_met
theorems.doc: A requirement with a missing input blocks REQUIREMENTS_MET.
theorems.statement: {rs : List Req} {r : Req} (hr : r ∈ rs) (h : Missing r) : verdict rs ≠ .met
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: verdict_append_notMet
theorems.doc: Adding requirements never turns NOT_MET into another verdict.
theorems.statement: {rs more : List Req} (h : verdict rs = .notMet) : verdict (rs ++ more) = .notMet
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: verdict_nil
theorems.doc: An empty check is vacuously met; the `spindrift-check` binary therefore refuses a check with no requirements.
theorems.statement: : verdict [] = .met
theorems.used_in: spindrift-check refuses a check with no requirements

theorems.name: Q.le_scale_left
theorems.doc: The order does not depend on the representation of the left number (scaling by `k > 0`).
theorems.statement: (a b : Q) (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) : Q.le ⟨a.num * k, a.den * k⟩ b ↔ Q.le a b
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Q.le_scale_right
theorems.doc: The order does not depend on the representation of the right number (scaling by `k > 0`).
theorems.statement: (a b : Q) (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) : Q.le a ⟨b.num * k, b.den * k⟩ ↔ Q.le a b
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Q.le_mul_self_iff
theorems.doc: Comparing squares is exact for non-negative numbers: `a² ≤ b² ↔ a ≤ b`. This is why the SNR requirement can be checked as `snr²·η²·BW ≤ A²·N` without square roots.
theorems.statement: (a b : Q) : Q.le (Q.mul a a) (Q.mul b b) ↔ Q.le a b
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: SNR requirements are checked in squared form, without square roots

theorems.name: Q.le_trans
theorems.doc: The order is transitive through a well-formed middle number.
theorems.statement: {a b c : Q} (hb : 0 < b.den) (h1 : Q.le a b) (h2 : Q.le b c) : Q.le a c
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Q.mul_comm
theorems.doc: The exact product does not depend on the order of the two numbers.
theorems.statement: (a b : Q) : Q.mul a b = Q.mul b a
theorems.tactics: simp only [Q.mul, Nat.mul_comm a.num b.num, Nat.mul_comm a.den b.den]
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Q.mul_le_mul_right
theorems.doc: Multiplying both sides by the same number on the right keeps the order.
theorems.statement: {a b : Q} (c : Q) (h : Q.le a b) : Q.le (Q.mul a c) (Q.mul b c)
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Q.mul_le_mul_left
theorems.doc: Multiplying both sides by the same number on the left keeps the order.
theorems.statement: {a b : Q} (c : Q) (h : Q.le a b) : Q.le (Q.mul c a) (Q.mul c b)
theorems.tactics: rw [Q.mul_comm c a, Q.mul_comm c b]
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Denotes.unique
theorems.doc: Exact products are unique.
theorems.statement: {fs : List (Option Q)} {p q : Q} (hp : Denotes fs p) (hq : Denotes fs q) : p = q
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: Denotes.replace_le
theorems.doc: Replacing one left-hand factor by a smaller well-formed one keeps an exact product (and makes it no larger).
theorems.statement: (l₁ : List (Option Q)) {l₂ : List (Option Q)} {x y p : Q} (h : Denotes (l₁ ++ some x :: l₂) p) (hy : 0 < y.den) (hyx : Q.le y x) : ∃ p', Denotes (l₁ ++ some y :: l₂) p' ∧ Q.le p' p
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: holds_mono_lhs
theorems.doc: A smaller left-hand factor never breaks a requirement that holds. This is why a datasheet upper bound (for example a noise density stated as `< 15 fT/√Hz`) may be used for that factor: if the requirement holds at the bound, it holds for every value below it.
theorems.statement: (id : String) (l₁ : List (Option Q)) {l₂ rhs : List (Option Q)} {x y : Q} (h : Holds ⟨id, l₁ ++ some x :: l₂, rhs⟩) (hy : 0 < y.den) (hyx : Q.le y x) : Holds ⟨id, l₁ ++ some y :: l₂, rhs⟩
theorems.tactics: obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hab⟩ := h
theorems.used_in: Verdict cards: the OPM SNR uses the datasheet noise bound (<15 fT/√Hz)

theorems.name: demo_met
theorems.doc: `1/2 ≤ 2/3` holds, so a one-requirement check is met.
theorems.statement: : verdict [⟨"demo", [some ⟨1, 2⟩], [some ⟨2, 3⟩]⟩] = .met
theorems.section: Worked examples, decided by the kernel
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: demo_notMet
theorems.doc: `3 ≤ 2` is violated, so the check is not met.
theorems.statement: : verdict [⟨"demo", [some ⟨3, 1⟩], [some ⟨2, 1⟩]⟩] = .notMet
theorems.section: Worked examples, decided by the kernel
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: demo_needInfo
theorems.doc: One missing factor and nothing violated: Lean asks for more information.
theorems.statement: : verdict [⟨"a", [none], [some ⟨2, 1⟩]⟩, ⟨"b", [some ⟨1, 1⟩], [some ⟨2, 1⟩]⟩] = .needInfo
theorems.section: Worked examples, decided by the kernel
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)

theorems.name: demo_notMet_beats_missing
theorems.doc: A violated requirement decides the verdict even when another one lacks an input.
theorems.statement: : verdict [⟨"a", [none], [some ⟨2, 1⟩]⟩, ⟨"b", [some ⟨3, 1⟩], [some ⟨2, 1⟩]⟩] = .notMet
theorems.section: Worked examples, decided by the kernel
theorems.used_in: Checker soundness (proved about SpinDrift.verdict, run by spindrift-check)
